chapter.name: Banks and the Magic of Finance

questions.q: Which type of bank account is a one-time deposit kept for a fixed period, such as 3 or 5 years?
questions.a: Fixed deposit account: the money is kept for a fixed period like 3 or 5 years, after which the bank returns it with interest.

questions.q: The chapter defines a bank as a financial institution that does two main things with money. Which pair is it?
o: It collects money as deposits and lends money as loans
It prints banknotes and fixes the benchmark interest rate
It buys and sells shares of companies for people
It builds roads and railway lines for the government
questions.a: A bank collects money from people as deposits and lends money to borrowers as loans.

questions.q: Match each term in Column A with its description in Column B. Column A: 1. Savings account  2. Current account  3. Fixed deposit account  4. Account holder. Column B: p. A person or business that has opened a bank account  q. Meant for businesses that make and receive many payments; earns no interest  r. Meant for individuals who save regularly; limits on how often money can be withdrawn each month  s. A one-time deposit kept for a fixed period
questions.a: 1-r, 2-q, 3-s, 4-p: savings account for regular savers with withdrawal limits, current account for businesses with no interest, fixed deposit for a one-time deposit, account holder for the person who opened the account.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Mrs Fernandes, who may need her money at short notice next month, should not put all of it in a 5-year fixed deposit. Reason (R): A fixed deposit usually earns higher interest than a savings account. Choose the correct option.
o: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A: she should avoid the fixed deposit because it is a one-time deposit kept for a fixed period such as 3 or 5 years, not because of its higher interest (which is an advantage).

questions.q: True or False: At the end of its fixed period, a fixed deposit returns the original amount along with interest. Give the verdict and then the reason.
questions.a: True. A fixed deposit is kept for a fixed period, like 3 or 5 years, and after that the bank returns the original amount plus interest, which is usually higher than a savings account offers.
s: Verdict: True
Reason: after the fixed period the bank returns the original amount plus interest (usually higher than on a savings account)

questions.q: A bank pays interest to people who keep money with it. (a) What does the bank do with the deposits, apart from keeping them safe? (b) How does this make it possible for the bank to pay interest to depositors?
questions.a: (a) The bank lends the deposited money to businesses and other people. (b) The borrowers pay interest to the bank on these loans, so the bank can give some extra money, interest, to the depositors over a regular period.
s: (a) States that the bank lends the deposits to businesses or other people
(b) Links it: borrowers pay interest on loans, out of which the bank pays interest to depositors

questions.q: (a) What is financial infrastructure? (b) Name any two parts of it given in the chapter. (c) Name one part of India's physical infrastructure whose building and upkeep financial infrastructure helps to fund.
questions.a: (a) Financial infrastructure is a network of banks, payment systems, stock markets and other financial institutions that help people, businesses and the government carry out financial transactions and manage money. (b) Any two of: banks, payment systems, stock markets, other financial institutions. (c) Any one of: roads, railways, telecommunication.
s: (a) Defines financial infrastructure as a network of banks, payment systems, stock markets and other institutions that help transactions and managing money
(b) Names two parts, such as banks and stock markets
(c) Names roads, railways or telecommunication

questions.q: Gauri says, 'A bank is useful only to people who have spare money to save; it does nothing for people who need money to run a business.' Do you agree? Give three points from the chapter to support your answer.
questions.a: No. She is right that banks help savers, but wrong that they do nothing for businesses. (1) Banks do help savers like Navdeep keep money safe and earn interest. (2) But the bank also gives Rima a loan for her bamboo business from the surplus money deposited by people like Navdeep. (3) Banks offer a current account meant for businesses and traders who make and receive many payments, and their services are used by shopkeepers, farmers and businesses, not only savers.
s: Verdict: disagrees, while accepting that banks do serve savers (safety and interest)
Uses Rima's bamboo business loan, funded from deposits like Navdeep's
Uses the current account for businesses and traders, or the range of users such as shopkeepers and farmers

questions.q: A bank branch in Guwahati puts up this notice. Savings account: interest 3% a year, opens with a minimum deposit, up to 5 withdrawals a month. Current account: no interest, no limit on the number of deposits and withdrawals. Fixed deposit for 3 years: interest 6.5% a year. Mrs Bora, a nurse, wants to save part of her salary every month and take out money now and then. Mr Kalita has ₹10,000 that he will not need for 3 years. (a) Which account should Mrs Bora open? (b) Which account pays nothing extra on money kept in it for a year? (c) How much interest will Mr Kalita's ₹10,000 earn in the first year in the fixed deposit? (d) Why might a shopkeeper still choose the account that pays no interest?
questions.a: (a) A savings account, since it is for individuals who save regularly and allows money to be added or withdrawn within limits. (b) The current account, which earns no interest. (c) 6.5% of ₹10,000 = ₹650. (d) Because a current account has no limit on how many times money can be deposited or withdrawn, which suits a shopkeeper who makes and receives payments many times.
s: (a) Savings account, with the reason that it suits a regular saver
(b) Current account
(d) No limit on deposits and withdrawals, which a shopkeeper making many payments needs

questions.q: Jasmeet, a nurse in Ludhiana, earns ₹18,000 a month. She spends about ₹6,000 a month and saves the rest. She will need some of her savings during the year, but ₹45,000 she will not touch for 3 years. Three plans are suggested to her: (i) keep all her savings as cash in a cupboard at home, (ii) put everything in a current account, (iii) keep the money she may need in a savings account and put the ₹45,000 in a fixed deposit. Evaluate each plan using the chapter and recommend one.
questions.a: (i) Cash at home is not safe, as Navdeep realised, and it earns no interest. (ii) A current account earns no interest and is meant for businesses and traders who make many payments; Jasmeet does not need unlimited transactions. (iii) A savings account suits an individual who saves regularly and needs to withdraw sometimes, and it earns interest. The ₹45,000 she will not need for 3 years fits a fixed deposit, a one-time deposit for a fixed period that usually earns higher interest than a savings account. Recommendation: plan (iii), because it keeps her money safe, lets her reach what she may need, and earns the most on money she will not touch.
s: Rejects plan (i): cash at home is unsafe and earns no interest
Rejects plan (ii): a current account earns no interest and is meant for businesses with many payments
Explains why a savings account suits the money she may need (interest, withdrawals allowed within limits)
Explains why the fixed deposit suits the ₹45,000 (fixed period, usually higher interest)
Recommends plan (iii) with a reasoned conclusion

questions.q: Gita deposits ₹500 in a bank that pays 6% interest a year. How much interest does she earn at the end of the first year?
questions.a: ₹30, since 6% of ₹500 = 6/100 × 500 = ₹30; ₹530 is the total amount, not the interest.

questions.q: What is the process of earning interest on previous interest called?
questions.a: Compounding: interest is earned not only on the original amount but also on the interest earned in previous years.

questions.q: Ashok's passbook shows a balance of ₹1,000. Then there is a credit of ₹2,000 on 1 March and a debit of ₹750 on 4 March. What is the balance after these two entries?
questions.a: ₹2,250: a credit is money received into the account and a debit is money taken out, so ₹1,000 + ₹2,000 − ₹750 = ₹2,250.

questions.q: In the story of the king and the sage, the first square of the chessboard holds 1 grain and the grains double on each square. Read the statements. I. The 9th square held 256 grains. II. The 16th square held 32,768 grains. III. The 10th square held 1,024 grains. Which of the statements is/are correct?
questions.a: I and II only: the 9th square had 256 and the 16th had 32,768 grains, but the 10th square had 512 grains; 1,024 was on the 11th square.

questions.q: (a) What is interest, as the chapter defines it? (b) Ravi deposits ₹1,800 in a bank at 4% interest a year. How much will he have at the end of one year?
questions.a: (a) Interest is the amount charged for borrowing money or the amount gained by lending money, usually expressed as a percentage. (b) ₹1,800 + 4% of ₹1,800 = ₹1,800 + ₹72 = ₹1,872.
s: (a) Interest: the amount charged for borrowing or gained by lending money, usually a percentage

questions.q: Zoya deposits ₹5,000 at 4% interest a year and withdraws nothing; the interest is added each year. (a) Find her amount at the end of 2 years. (b) How much more is this than she would have if interest were paid only on the original ₹5,000 each year?
questions.a: (a) Year 1: 4% of ₹5,000 = ₹200, amount ₹5,200. Year 2: 4% of ₹5,200 = ₹208, amount ₹5,408. (b) With interest only on ₹5,000 she would have ₹5,000 + ₹200 + ₹200 = ₹5,400, so compounding gives ₹8 more, the interest on the first year's ₹200 interest.
s: (a) ₹5,408, using ₹200 in year 1 and ₹208 in year 2
(b) ₹8 more than ₹5,400, explained as interest on the previous interest

questions.q: Sunil's bank passbook has two new lines: 'Salary received ₹15,000' and 'School fee paid ₹4,000'. (a) What is a passbook? (b) His balance before these two lines was ₹2,500. Using the meaning of credit and debit, find his balance after both lines. (c) Where can a passbook be updated?
questions.a: (a) A diary-like document given by the bank that keeps a record of all the receipts and payment transactions in an account. (b) The salary is a credit (money received), so it is added; the school fee is a debit (money taken out), so it is subtracted: ₹2,500 + ₹15,000 − ₹4,000 = ₹13,500. (c) At the bank, where it can be updated regularly.
s: (a) A diary-like record, given by the bank, of all receipts and payments
(b) ₹13,500, adding the credit and subtracting the debit
(c) At the bank, regularly

questions.q: On the sage's chessboard the first square holds 1 grain and each square holds double the one before it. (a) On which square does the number of grains first go above one thousand? (b) On which square does it first go above one lakh? (c) The chapter says that the 32nd square held over 210 crore grains. Check this claim by working out the grains on that square.
questions.a: (a) The 10th square has 512 and the 11th has 1,024, so the 11th square is the first above one thousand. (b) The 17th square has 65,536 and the 18th has 1,31,072, so the 18th square is the first above one lakh. (c) The 32nd square has 2 multiplied by itself 31 times = 2,14,74,83,648 grains, about 214.7 crore, which is indeed over 210 crore.
s: (a) The 11th square (1,024 grains, after 512 on the 10th)
(b) The 18th square (1,31,072 grains, after 65,536 on the 17th)
(c) 2,14,74,83,648 grains, about 214.7 crore, confirming over 210 crore

questions.q: Meher receives ₹3,000 as a prize and deposits it in a bank that pays 10% interest a year. She withdraws nothing, so each year's interest is added to her money. She wants to buy a bicycle costing ₹4,000 at the end of 3 years using only this deposit. Work out her amount at the end of the first, second and third years, and decide whether the deposit alone will pay for the bicycle.
questions.a: Year 1: 10% of ₹3,000 = ₹300, amount ₹3,300. Year 2: 10% of ₹3,300 = ₹330, amount ₹3,630. Year 3: 10% of ₹3,630 = ₹363, amount ₹3,993. Decision: ₹3,993 is less than ₹4,000, so the deposit alone falls short by ₹7 and she must add a little more money.
s: Year 1 amount ₹3,300
Year 2 amount ₹3,630 (interest ₹330)
Year 3 amount ₹3,993 (interest ₹363)
Decides it is not enough: ₹7 short of ₹4,000

questions.q: Ira deposits ₹2,400 in a bank at 5% interest a year and does not withdraw anything. (a) How much interest does she earn in the first year? (b) What is her amount at the end of the first year? (c) How much interest does she earn in the second year? (d) Why is the second year's interest more than the first year's? (e) Which document given by the bank records her deposits and withdrawals?
questions.a: (a) 5% of ₹2,400 = ₹120. (b) ₹2,400 + ₹120 = ₹2,520. (c) 5% of ₹2,520 = ₹126. (d) Because in the second year interest is earned on ₹2,520, which includes the first year's interest; this is compounding. (e) The passbook.
s: (d) Interest is earned on the previous interest too (compounding)
(e) The passbook

questions.q: According to the chapter, what is a loan?
o: An amount borrowed from a bank or financial institution that must be repaid with interest later
Money placed in a bank account that can be withdrawn and often earns interest
A gift of money from the bank that never has to be returned
A part-ownership in a company bought at the stock exchange
questions.a: A loan is an amount borrowed from banks or financial institutions, with the obligation to repay it with interest at a later time.

questions.q: A bank pays 3% a year on a deposit of ₹1,000 and lends the same ₹1,000 for one year at 8%. How much does the bank earn from this?
questions.a: ₹50: the borrower pays ₹80 (8% of ₹1,000) as interest, the bank pays the depositor ₹30 (3% of ₹1,000), and the difference of ₹50 is the bank's income.

questions.q: Over 50 crore bank accounts have been opened under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana. By whom, mainly, were they opened?
o: Mainly by people who already had a bank account
questions.a: Mainly by women, according to the chapter.

questions.q: Assertion (A): The difference between the interest on loans and the interest on deposits is a source of income for banks. Reason (R): Banks pay a higher rate of interest on savings deposits than they charge on loans. Choose the correct option.
o: A is true, but R is false.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.a: A is true, but R is false: banks pay a lower rate on savings deposits and charge a higher rate on loans, and that difference is their income.

questions.q: True or False: The Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana was launched in 2014 mainly for large businesses that already had bank accounts. Give the verdict and then the corrected statement.
questions.a: False. The Jan Dhan Yojana, launched in 2014, aimed to give every Indian, especially low-income earners, a bank account without needing a minimum balance or fees.
s: Verdict: False
Correction: it aimed to give every Indian, especially low-income earners, an account with no minimum balance or fees

questions.q: (a) Give one purpose for which a family may take a loan from a bank. (b) Give one purpose for which a business may take a loan.
questions.a: (a) Any one: buying a house, buying a vehicle, funding education. (b) Any one: buying new machinery, buying raw materials, transporting products, launching new products in markets.
s: (a) A household purpose such as a house, a vehicle or education
(b) A business purpose such as machinery, raw materials, transport or launching a product

questions.q: Kiran deposits ₹500 in a bank that pays her 2% a year. The bank lends this ₹500 to Manoj for one year at 6%. (a) How much does Manoj repay in all? (b) How much does the bank earn after paying Kiran?
questions.a: (a) Manoj repays ₹500 + 6% of ₹500 = ₹500 + ₹30 = ₹530. (b) The bank pays Kiran ₹500 + ₹10 = ₹510, so it earns ₹530 − ₹510 = ₹20.
s: (a) ₹530 (₹500 loan + ₹30 interest)
(b) ₹20 (₹530 received − ₹510 paid to Kiran)

questions.q: Since the Jan Dhan Yojana, more people use banking services. (a) How do workers now receive their wages? (b) How do students who do well receive their scholarships? (c) What two benefits does the chapter say such direct transfers bring?
questions.a: (a) Workers receive their wages directly into their bank accounts. (b) Scholarships from institutions are paid into the students' bank accounts. (c) Direct transfers have reduced middlemen and ensure the timely disbursement of funds.
s: (a) Wages paid directly into bank accounts
(b) Scholarships paid into the students' accounts
(c) Fewer middlemen and timely payment of funds

questions.q: A bank branch in Indore holds deposits of ₹6,00,000, on which it pays 3% interest a year. It charges 8% a year on the loans it gives. At the end of the year its income from the difference in interest is ₹22,000. Find the interest it pays its depositors, the interest it must have received on its loans, and how much it lent. Then find how much it kept aside and explain why a bank does this.
questions.a: Interest paid to depositors = 3% of ₹6,00,000 = ₹18,000. Income = interest received − interest paid, so interest received = ₹22,000 + ₹18,000 = ₹40,000. This is 8% of the amount lent, so amount lent = ₹40,000 ÷ 8% = ₹5,00,000. Kept aside = ₹6,00,000 − ₹5,00,000 = ₹1,00,000. The chapter says banks have reserve money and do not lend all the deposits as loans; keeping some back also lets the bank pay depositors who withdraw.
s: Interest paid to depositors ₹18,000
Interest received on loans ₹22,000 + ₹18,000 = ₹40,000
Kept aside ₹1,00,000, as banks keep reserve money and do not lend all deposits (accept also: so that depositors who withdraw can be paid)

questions.q: Lata deposits ₹1,000 for a year in a bank that pays 3% interest. The bank lends it for that year at 7% to Ramesh, a potter, who buys a new wheel for his workshop. Evaluate the claim, 'In this arrangement everyone gains and no one pays anything extra.' Use the figures and the chapter.
questions.a: Lata gains: she gets ₹1,000 + ₹30 = ₹1,030. The bank gains: it receives ₹1,000 + ₹70 = ₹1,070 from Ramesh and pays ₹1,030, earning ₹40 from the interest difference. Ramesh gains a wheel he could not afford on his own, but he pays ₹70 extra as interest. So the first part is fair (all three can benefit), but the second part is wrong: the borrower pays interest, and the arrangement helps him only if his business earns more than the ₹70 he pays. The claim is partly right.
s: Lata receives ₹1,030 (₹30 interest)
Ramesh repays ₹1,070, paying ₹70 interest
The bank earns ₹40 from the difference in interest rates
Points out that the borrower does pay extra and gains only if his business earns more than the interest
Concludes the claim is partly right, with reasons

questions.q: Which of the following is a savings scheme offered by Indian post offices?
questions.a: Kisan Vikas Patra, along with National Savings Certificates and Sukanya Samriddhi accounts, is a post office savings scheme.

questions.q: In which year was the Reserve Bank of India established?
questions.a: 1935; it has functioned as the banker of banks, the central bank, since 1949.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the works of the Reserve Bank of India described in the chapter?
o: Funding businesses in areas like power and textiles
Maintaining the accounts of other banks
Giving loans to banks and the government
Setting rules on printing and distributing banknotes
questions.a: Funding businesses in areas like power and textiles is the work of the Industrial Finance Corporation of India, not the RBI.

questions.q: Read the statements about temples as banks in ancient India. I. Temples accepted public deposits just like modern banks. II. Contracts between the temples and borrowers were etched on copper plates. III. A 13th-century inscription from Kodumbalur in Tamil Nadu refers to communities that borrowed from a temple and agreed to pay interest. Which of the statements is/are correct?
questions.a: II and III only: temples lent money to artisans, merchants and local governments, but they did not accept public deposits like modern banks.

questions.q: Assertion (A): The Reserve Bank of India can be compared to Kubera, the God of Wealth. Reason (R): The RBI has the sole right of issuing currency and is the banker to banks. Choose the correct option.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.a: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A: the chapter compares the RBI to Kubera because of its sole right to issue currency and its role as banker to banks.

questions.q: (a) What is the full name of NABARD? (b) How does it support rural development?
questions.a: (a) National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development. (b) It funds banks that give loans for farming, village industries and infrastructure like roads and irrigation.
s: (a) National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
(b) Funds banks that give loans for farming, village industries, roads and irrigation

questions.q: Both NABARD and the Reserve Bank of India give money to banks. Differentiate between them on (a) the purpose for which each gives funds and (b) who else, besides banks, receives loans from the RBI.
questions.a: (a) NABARD funds banks so that they can give loans for farming, village industries and rural infrastructure; the RBI, as banker of banks, keeps accounts of banks, helps exchange funds between them and lends to them while supervising the whole banking system. (b) The RBI also provides loans to the government.
s: (a) NABARD funds banks for rural loans, while the RBI lends to banks as the banker of banks that supervises the system
(b) The government also borrows from the RBI

questions.q: Tina says, 'Post offices only deliver letters and parcels; they have no part in India's financial infrastructure.' Do you agree? Give three points from the chapter.
questions.a: No. (1) Post offices offer financial services, including savings schemes such as National Savings Certificates, Kisan Vikas Patra and Sukanya Samriddhi accounts. (2) Their vast network reaches even remote locations where banks may not be near. (3) This makes them a popular savings option, so they are one of the other financial institutions apart from banks.
s: Disagrees and names post office savings schemes such as NSC, Kisan Vikas Patra or Sukanya Samriddhi
Uses their vast network that reaches remote locations
Concludes they are a popular savings option and part of the financial institutions besides banks

questions.q: A business newspaper from Mumbai printed this report on one week of the Reserve Bank of India's work: 'On Monday the RBI gave the Government of India a short-term loan of ₹2,000 crore. On Tuesday a bank in Kolkata deposited ₹300 crore of its spare funds in the account it keeps with the RBI. On Wednesday the RBI moved funds from the account that one bank keeps with it to the account that another bank keeps with it.' (a) What is the RBI also called, since it supervises India's banking system? (b) Which event in the report shows the RBI lending to the government? (c) Which two events show the RBI acting as the banker to banks? (d) Since which year has the RBI been functioning as the banker of banks?
questions.a: (a) India's central bank. (b) Monday's short-term loan of ₹2,000 crore to the Government of India. (c) Tuesday's deposit of ₹300 crore by the Kolkata bank into the account it keeps with the RBI, and Wednesday's transfer of funds between the accounts that banks keep with the RBI. (d) Since 1949.
s: (a) India's central bank
(b) The ₹2,000 crore loan to the Government of India
(c) The Kolkata bank's deposit in its account with the RBI and the transfer of funds between banks' accounts

questions.q: A district officer in Jharkhand has three needs: (i) a retired mill worker in a small town wants a safe government savings scheme close to his home; (ii) a women's group wants a loan to start a pickle-making unit, a village industry; (iii) a company wants funds to build a solar power plant. A planner says, 'The Reserve Bank of India should directly handle all three, because it is the most important bank.' Evaluate this plan and suggest a better one using the chapter.
questions.a: The plan is weak. (i) Post offices, with their vast network even in small and remote places, offer savings schemes such as National Savings Certificates and Kisan Vikas Patra accounts, which suit the retired worker. (ii) NABARD funds banks that give loans for village industries, so the women's group should borrow from a bank supported by NABARD. (iii) The Industrial Finance Corporation of India funds businesses in areas like power, so it suits the solar power company. The RBI's role is different: it is the banker to banks and the government, keeps banks' accounts, lends to them and sets rules on currency and benchmark rates; it supervises the system rather than serving each person or firm. So a better plan sends each need to its own institution under the RBI's supervision.
s: (i) A post office savings scheme such as NSC for the retired worker
(ii) A bank loan supported by NABARD for the village industry
(iii) The Industrial Finance Corporation of India for the power plant
Explains the RBI's actual role as banker to banks and the government that supervises and sets rules
Judges the planner's idea wrong and states the better plan

questions.q: What does ATM stand for?
questions.a: Automated Teller Machine, a self-service machine available 24×7 from which cash can be withdrawn with a debit card and PIN.

questions.q: Which organisation launched the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) in 2016?
o: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)
questions.a: The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) launched UPI in 2016.

questions.q: Kavita pays a shopkeeper by scanning his QR code with a UPI app on her phone. Her brother logs in to their bank's website on his computer, checks the account balance and transaction history, and transfers money to another account. Which statement about the two tools is correct?
o: Kavita uses UPI-based mobile payment and her brother uses internet banking.
Both of them use internet banking, because both payments go over the internet.
Kavita uses internet banking and her brother uses UPI-based mobile payment.
Both of them use UPI, because both move money digitally.
questions.a: Kavita uses UPI-based mobile payment (paying through a QR code) and her brother uses internet banking (checking balances and transaction history and transferring money through the bank's website).

questions.q: Match each item in Column A with its description in Column B. Column A: 1. PIN  2. POS machine  3. QR code  4. Cheque book. Column B: p. Scanned with a phone app to pay through UPI  q. A numeric code, usually 4 to 6 digits, used for security  r. Given by the bank, it holds several paper instruments for paying from an account  s. A machine at a shop where a debit card is swiped or inserted to pay
questions.a: 1-q, 2-s, 3-p, 4-r: a PIN is a numeric security code, a POS machine takes debit card payments at shops, a QR code is scanned to pay by UPI, and a cheque book holds the bank's paper cheques.

questions.q: True or False: Nepal was the first country to adopt India's UPI as a payment platform. Give the verdict and then the reason.
questions.a: True. The chapter says Nepal adopted UPI in 2022, becoming the first country to do so; other nations such as the United Arab Emirates, France, Sri Lanka, Bhutan and Mauritius have adopted it since.
s: Verdict: True
Reason: Nepal adopted UPI in 2022, the first country to do so

questions.q: When Anjali pays Dinesh, a tea seller, by scanning his QR code, these steps happen, but they are jumbled: P. NPCI verifies the UPI PIN and processes the transfer. Q. The payer's bank forwards the request to NPCI. R. The app sends a payment request to the payer's bank. S. The payee's bank receives the funds. (a) Write the steps in the correct order. (b) After scanning the QR code, what two things must Anjali enter in the app before step R can happen?
questions.a: (a) R, Q, P, S: the app sends the request to Anjali's bank, the bank forwards it to NPCI, NPCI verifies the PIN and processes the transfer, and Dinesh's bank receives the funds. (b) The amount to be sent and her UPI PIN.
s: (a) Correct order R, Q, P, S
(b) The amount and her UPI PIN

questions.q: (a) Name the two ways, given in the chapter, of withdrawing savings from a bank account. (b) Name any two public places where ATMs are found. (c) What does PIN stand for?
questions.a: (a) Filling out a withdrawal slip and submitting it at the bank's cash counter, or using a debit card at an ATM. (b) Any two: bus depots, local shopping markets, railway stations, airports, malls. (c) Personal Identification Number.
s: (a) Withdrawal slip at the cash counter, and debit card at an ATM
(b) Two places such as railway stations and airports
(c) Personal Identification Number

questions.q: Mr Rao, in Vijayawada, must pay ₹12,000 rent to his landlord, who lives in Chennai, before midnight tonight. He has a cheque book, a debit card and a UPI app linked to his account. Which of these can get the money into the landlord's account in time, and why can each of the other two not do it?
questions.a: The UPI app can, because UPI transfers money instantly using the payee's phone number or QR code. A cheque cannot, because it must be handed over and deposited at a bank, which needs a physical visit and takes time. The debit card cannot do it here, because the chapter describes it for withdrawing cash at an ATM or paying at a shop's POS machine, and the landlord is far away with no POS machine.
s: Chooses UPI because it transfers money instantly by phone number or QR code
Rejects the cheque: it needs a visit to the bank and takes time
Rejects the debit card: it is used at an ATM or a shop's POS machine, which does not reach the distant landlord

questions.q: Asha has to pay ₹3,750 to Vikram Traders by cheque for a cupboard. Using the parts of a cheque shown in the chapter, describe what she must fill in on the cheque before handing it over, and explain what happens to the money after Vikram Traders deposits the cheque in its bank.
questions.a: She writes the date on which she issues the cheque and the name of the person to be paid, Vikram Traders. She writes the amount both in words (three thousand seven hundred and fifty rupees) and in numbers (₹3,750). She signs in the place for the cheque issuer's signature. After Vikram Traders deposits the cheque, ₹3,750 is withdrawn (debited) from Asha's account and transferred (credited) to Vikram Traders' account.
s: Writes the date and the payee's name, Vikram Traders
Writes the amount in words and in numbers
Signs in the issuer's signature space
Explains the debit from Asha's account and the credit to Vikram Traders' account

questions.q: Sameer buys fruit at a market stall and pays by scanning the vendor's QR code with a payment app on his phone. (a) Which payment system does such an app use? (b) Name the app based on this system that the chapter mentions. (c) Besides a QR code, what can he use to identify the person he is paying? (d) What secret code must Sameer enter before the payment goes through? (e) Why did this way of paying become popular during the COVID-19 pandemic?
questions.a: (a) The Unified Payments Interface (UPI). (b) BHIM (Bharat Interface for Money). (c) The phone number of the recipient. (d) His UPI PIN. (e) Because it supports cashless transactions, which helped people keep social distancing during the pandemic.
s: (a) UPI
(b) BHIM
(c) The recipient's phone number
(d) The UPI PIN
(e) It supports cashless payment, helping social distancing during COVID-19

questions.q: According to the chapter, what is a share?
o: A unit of ownership in a company
A loan that a bank gives to a company
A payment made through a UPI app
The interest earned on a fixed deposit
questions.a: A share is a unit of ownership in a company; buying one makes a person a part-owner of that company.

questions.q: The share prices of a large number of companies rise at the same time. What is this called?
questions.a: A stock market boom; a fall in the share prices of many companies together is a crash.

questions.q: Read the statements. I. The Bombay Stock Exchange was established in 1875 and is one of the oldest stock exchanges in the world. II. Share transactions at the stock exchange are still done today mainly with paper tickets. III. A financial fraud can be reported on the helpline 1930. Which of the statements is/are correct?
questions.a: I and III only: paper tickets were used in earlier days, but they have been replaced by digital transactions using advanced computers.

questions.q: Assertion (A): Once a share has been issued, its price stays fixed. Reason (R): Share prices rise and fall because of factors such as a company's performance and government policy changes. Choose the correct option.
o: A is false, but R is true.
A is true, but R is false.
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.a: A is false, but R is true: like commodity prices, share prices rise and fall, due to a company's performance, government policy, tax rules, political instability, wars or economic shocks.

questions.q: True or False: A One-Time Password (OTP) stays the same for every payment, so it is fine to write it down and keep it for later use. Give the verdict and then the reason.
questions.a: False. An OTP is a unique, temporary code of letters or numbers used for verifying identity or authorising a transaction, so it does not stay the same; and OTPs should never be shared with strangers, since fraudsters use them to drain bank accounts.
s: Verdict: False
Reason: an OTP is a unique temporary code for verifying identity or authorising a transaction (and is never shared)

questions.q: A company has issued 2,000 shares in all. (a) Ritu wants to own 5% of the company. How many shares must she hold? (b) Her cousin Aman holds 300 shares. What percentage of the company does he own, and who is the bigger part-owner of the two?
questions.a: (a) 5% of 2,000 = 100 shares. (b) 300 out of 2,000 = 15%; Aman is the bigger part-owner, because the more shares a person owns, the higher the ownership in the company.
s: (b) 15%; Aman, since more shares mean higher ownership

questions.q: Answer from the chapter's advice on staying safe while making digital payments. (a) Name any two pieces of personal information that should never be shared with strangers. (b) What should you avoid clicking on? (c) Where can a fraud be reported?
questions.a: (a) Any two: phone number, account number, home address, passwords, OTPs. (b) Unknown links or videos received through messages. (c) The helpline 1930 or the National Cybercrime Reporting Portal.
s: (a) Two items such as the account number and OTPs
(b) Unknown links or videos received in messages
(c) Helpline 1930 or the National Cybercrime Reporting Portal

questions.q: Read three news headlines: (i) 'Floods shut roads and factories across the state'; (ii) 'Customers return Chirag Biscuits' new biscuit after complaints about its taste'; (iii) 'Government announces new tax rules for cement makers'. For each headline, say whether the cause lies inside a company, with the government, or outside both, and explain how it can make share prices fall.
questions.a: (i) Outside both: floods are a natural disaster, an economic shock, which can make share prices fall. (ii) Inside the company: a bad product means fewer people want Chirag Biscuits' shares, so its share price drops. (iii) With the government: a policy change such as new tax rules can make the share prices of the cement makers fall.
s: (i) Outside event: floods are an economic shock that can lower share prices
(ii) Company problem: a bad product lowers demand for its shares
(iii) Government: new tax rules are a policy change that can lower share prices

questions.q: In one month the share price of Narmada Foods rose from ₹400 to ₹460 after it launched a popular new product. In the same month the share price of Sahyadri Motors fell from ₹250 to ₹210 after a long workers' strike. News reports said that the share prices of most companies on the exchange rose that month. Raghav owns 20 shares of Narmada Foods and 30 shares of Sahyadri Motors. (a) By how much did the value of Raghav's Narmada Foods shares change? (b) By how much did the value of his Sahyadri Motors shares change? (c) What was his overall gain or loss for the month? (d) What was the market as a whole going through that month, and does Raghav's result show that every shareholder gains in such a month? Explain.
questions.a: (a) Rise of ₹60 a share × 20 = ₹1,200 gain. (b) Fall of ₹40 a share × 30 = ₹1,200 loss. (c) ₹1,200 − ₹1,200 = no overall gain or loss. (d) A stock market boom, since the prices of most companies rose together; but Raghav gained nothing, because one company's own problem, the strike, lowered its share price even in a boom, so not every shareholder gains in a boom.
s: (a) ₹1,200 gain on Narmada Foods
(b) ₹1,200 loss on Sahyadri Motors
(c) No overall gain or loss
(d) Identifies a boom and explains that a company's own problem can still lower its price, so not every shareholder gains

questions.q: Dadaji has just started using UPI. He tells the family his plan: (i) if a caller says he has won a prize and must download an app to claim it, he will download the app; (ii) he will share his home address and bank account number with a friendly stranger in an online group who has promised to send him a gift; (iii) if he is ever cheated, he will keep quiet, since nothing can be done. Evaluate each part of his plan using the chapter, and then give him one more safety habit the chapter advises.
questions.a: (i) Unsafe: fraudsters use fake calls to trick people into downloading harmful apps, which give them access to the phone so they can steal personal data and drain money from bank accounts. (ii) Unsafe: personal information such as the home address and account number should never be shared with strangers. (iii) Wrong: a fraud should be reported on the helpline 1930 or the National Cybercrime Reporting Portal. So every part of the plan must change. One more habit: do not store sensitive banking information such as passwords and debit card PINs on devices (or avoid clicking unknown links received in messages).
s: (i) Rejects downloading the app, since fake calls get harmful apps installed to steal data and money
(ii) Rejects sharing the address and account number with strangers
(iii) Says the fraud should be reported on 1930 or the National Cybercrime Reporting Portal
Judges that the whole plan is unsafe and must change
Gives one more habit from the chapter, such as not storing PINs or passwords on devices
